adversary

/AD-ver-ser-ee/ — stress on first syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

An adversary is a person or group that opposes or fights against someone else.

The knight faced his fiercest adversary in the final battle.

Example

In the chess tournament, the young player finally faced the grandmaster she had studied for months — her greatest adversary in the competition, a player who had dominated the field for years.

Adversary is more than just a rival; it captures someone actively opposing you in a conflict or competition. 'Opponent' is plainer, but adversary suggests a more serious, perhaps more skilled or dangerous opposing force.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

challenger: A challenger is the one who steps forward to start a contest — the boxer calling out the titleholder, the newcomer running against the mayor. The word tells you who began the fight, not how bitter it is. An adversary is anyone set against you in a serious struggle, whoever started it.

competitor: A competitor is someone striving to win the same prize you want — a race, a contract, a title. Competition needs no hatred, and competitors can shake hands afterward. An adversary opposes you directly, and the word carries real conflict and hostility, not just a shared goal.

combatant: A combatant is a person actively fighting in a battle — the fighting has already begun. An adversary can oppose you before and without any physical fight at all: two lawyers arguing a lawsuit are adversaries, but no one would call them combatants.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

partner: someone working alongside you toward shared goals

ally: a supporter joined with you against others

Where it sits · how serious and hostile the conflict is — opponent → rival → foe → adversary

opponent vs. adversary: An opponent is the weakest word on this scale — simply anyone on the other side of a game or debate — much milder than an adversary, who actively works against you.

rival vs. adversary: A rival competes with you again and again for the same goal, but the word is still weaker than adversary, which adds a sense of real opposition and hostility.

foe vs. adversary: A foe is a true enemy, coming close in force to adversary, yet adversary is slightly stronger and more formal, naming someone deliberately set against you in a serious struggle.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-

Prefix — ad-: to, toward (here: turned toward, hence against)

Root — vers

Root — vers: to turn (from Latin vertere/versus, 'turned') (Latin)

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: a person connected with; one who

Put it together

Put it together: Ad- means 'toward,' vers means 'turned,' and -ary names a person — so an adversary is literally 'one who has turned toward you' in confrontation. That is exactly why an adversary is a person or group that opposes or fights against someone else.

Use the root in a new word: avert

Use the root in a new word: avert: When the movie got scary, Maya averted her eyes, turning them away from the screen.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal

Adversary is a formal, serious word for an opponent in conflict. Use it when the opposition is genuine and the stakes feel real — legal disputes, competitions, struggles. For everyday use, 'opponent' works fine, but adversary brings gravity and formality to the conflict.
